Problem numbers refer to the textbook (Chiang & Wainwright, 4th edition). These are not graded, but you should attempt them all before the quiz. Try each part yourself first, then expand the **Solution** to check.

## Exercise 4.6

**6.** Let $A=I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T$.

a. Must $A$ be square? Must $\left(X^T X\right)$ be square? Must $X$ be square?

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

Say the dimension of $X$ is $m \times n$. Then the dimension of $X^T_{n \times m} X_{m \times n}$ is $n \times n$, so the dimension of $\left(X^T X\right)^{-1}$ is also $n \times n$. This implies that the dimension of $X_{m \times n}\left(X^T X\right)^{-1}_{n \times n} X^T_{n \times m}$ is $m \times m$. Hence, $X^T X$ and $A$ must be square matrices, but $X$ need not be square.

</details>

b. Show that matrix $A$ is idempotent.

<details class="solution part">
<summary>Solution</summary>

To prove a matrix is idempotent, we need to show $AA=A$:
$$\begin{aligned}
A A &= (I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T)(I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T) \\
& = I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T+X\underbrace{\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T X}_{I}\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T \\
&= I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T+X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T \\
&= I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T = A
\end{aligned}$$

</details>
